blocks.en: Abstract
blocks.zh: 摘要

blocks.en: Text-conditioned hand-object interaction (HOI) generation provides intuitive semantic control, but language is an indirect way to specify where an interaction should occur on an object. Naming the part to grasp requires object-specific words, and naming the approach side requires a reference frame that a prompt lacks. We propose GRAZE (GRAsp from gaZE), which generates hand-object grasp motion from recorded gaze instead of object and part names. Its Geometry-Aware Gaze Encoding (GeoGaze) maps gaze rays to cues on object geometry, and cross-attention conditions a diffusion Transformer on these cues. We also introduce HOT3D-Grasp, a grasp-centered benchmark with object-disjoint folds built on HOT3D recordings. On unseen objects, GRAZE grasps the target part more often than the strongest text-conditioned baseline (49.3% vs. 43.6%), achieves the highest grasp success (66.3% vs. 46.6%), and transfers without fine-tuning to GazeHOI (45.3% vs. 33.8%). Gaze conveys the approach side: when gaze is rotated around the object, the approach turns with it in 59.1% of cases, against 20.5% for a text model retrained with clock words. On the same backbone, a text prompt names parts better, but gaze adds the approach side. Given both, GRAZE keeps the prompt's part accuracy and follows gaze.
blocks.zh: 文本有条件的手-对象交互(HOI)生成提供了直观语义控制,但语言是一种间接的方式来指定一个对象上应当发生交互的地方. 命名要抓取的部分需要针对对象的单词,命名取向方需要一个提示所缺少的参考框架. 我们提出GRAZE(GRASP from gaZE),它从记录的目光而不是物体和部分名称产生手取物运动. 它的几何- Aware Gaze Encoding (GeoGaze) 将凝视射线映射到物体几何上的提示, 并且交叉视线条件 扩散变形器在这些提示上。 我们还引入了HOT3D-Grasp,这是以HOT3D录音为基础,以对象分解折叠为抓取性基准. 在看不见的物体上,GRAZE比最强的文本条件基线(49.3%对43.6%)更经常地掌握目标部分,取得最高的把握成功(66.3%对46.6%),没有向GazeHOI进行微调(45.3%对33.8%)。 Gaze传达了取向的一面:在围绕物体旋转时,取向在59.1%的情况下随取向而转出,而文本模型则有20.5%重新用时钟词来调整. 在同一条主干线上,文字提示名称部分更好,但凝视增加了接近的一面. 鉴于这两种情况,GRAZE保持了提示部分的准确性并跟踪视线.

blocks.en: 1 Introduction
blocks.zh: 导言

blocks.en: Generating realistic hand–object interaction (HOI) motion is essential for animating hands in virtual and mixed reality. Recent generative models synthesize HOI motion from a text prompt [ 5 , 9 , 24 , 18 , 38 , 8 , 33 , 44 ] . Earlier methods needed the wrist or object trajectory as input [ 49 ] , whereas a prompt only has to describe what the hand should do, such as “grab the handle of the mug.”
blocks.zh: 产生现实的手-对象交互(HOI)运动对于虚拟和混合现实中的动画手至关重要. 近期的基因模型从文本提示合成HOI运动[5,9,24,18,38,8,33,44]. 早期的方法需要手腕或物体轨迹作为输入 [49] ,而一个提示只需描述手应该做什么,例如“抓起杯子的手柄”。

blocks.en: Yet language is not always the most direct control signal for grasping. Text conveys semantic intention , such as the object category and the action, but grasping also requires spatial intention : which object to approach and where to contact it. Text-conditioned methods such as Text2HOI infer contact from the prompt and the object geometry, so the user has no direct way to specify the grasp location [ 5 ] . Words fall short in three cases. First, these models observe objects only as geometry, so an appearance word cannot separate similarly shaped objects ( a). Second, a part name such as a dumbbell’s “head” may refer to two symmetric instances, and “left” or “right” cannot pick one because these words depend on an unstated viewpoint: the same head is on the left from one side of the table and on the right from the other ( b). Third, the same part name ( e.g . , handle) denotes differently shaped regions on different objects, so the prompt does not identify the intended grasp location ( c).
blocks.zh: 然而,语言并不总是最直接的控制信号。 文本传达语义意图,例如对象类别和动作,但抓住还需要空间意图 :哪个对象接近和在哪里联系. Text2HOI从提示和对象几何推断接触等文字条件化的方法,因此用户无法直接指定抓取位置[5]. 三例中言语不足. 首先,这些模型只作为几何观测对象,因此一个外观词不能将类似形状的物体(a)分开. 第二,诸如哑铃的 " 头 " 这样的部分名称可能指两个对称的事例, " 左 " 或 " 右 " 无法选择一个,因为这些词取决于一个未表述的观点:同一个头在桌子的左边,另一个(b)在右边。 第三,同一部分名称(如:手柄)在不同物体上表示不同形状的区域,因此提示符没有识别预期的抓取位置(c).

blocks.en: These cases concern where to grasp. Text also leaves the approach side unspecified. This side matters in real scenes: if the handle of a mug faces away from the person, the hand must reach around the mug or first turn it, so a plausible grasp motion depends on how the object is rotated relative to the person. The object can lie in any pose relative to the person, but text-conditioned methods never observe where the person stands. Adding a direction word does not help: a user’s “3 o’clock” has no reference frame in the scene, and even a text model retrained with object-frame clock words turns its approach to match a changed word no more often than a random direction (25%, Figs. d and 5 b).
blocks.zh: 这些案件涉及如何掌握。 文本还未指明接近方。 这个侧面在真实的场景中很重要:如果一个杯子的手柄面朝人走开,手必须伸到杯子周围或者先翻转,所以一个可信的抓取动作取决于物体相对于个人的旋转方式. 对象可以停留在任何相对于人物的姿势中,但文字条件化的方法从不观察人物的位置. 添加一个方向词无济于事:一个用户的"3:00"在现场没有参考框架,甚至一个用对象框钟词重新训练的文本模型也会改变它的方法,以匹配一个变化的词,不过是一个随机方向(25%,Figs.d和5b).

blocks.en: These limitations motivate an input that needs no object or part names and carries spatial information that words express poorly, such as where the person is relative to the object. Human gaze provides such an input: people typically look toward an intended object or region before and during interaction [ 32 , 20 , 30 , 1 , 3 ] . Gaze does not define a complete hand trajectory, but it offers two spatial cues for grasp generation: where the ray meets the object marks the intended part, and where the ray starts, at the eye, tells which side of the object faces the person. Gaze is also cheap to obtain: the eye tracker of an egocentric headset records it without annotation.
blocks.zh: 这些限制激发了一个不需要对象或部分名称的输入,并携带文字表达不良的空间信息,例如人物相对于对象的位置. 人类的目光提供了这种投入:人们通常在互动之前和互动期间向预定物体或区域看[32、20、30、1、3]。 Gaze没有定义完整的手轨,但它为抓取生成提供了两个空间提示:射线与物体相遇时标出预定部分,射线从哪里开始,在眼睛上告诉物体的哪一边面对人. 盖兹也便宜地获得:一个以自我为中心的耳机的眼睛跟踪器不加注释地记录它.

blocks.en:
In this paper, we propose GRAZE (GRAsp from gaZE), a gaze-guided framework for generating
grasp-based HOI motion toward the object region the person looks at. Given the object’s geometry, its initial pose, and the first 30% of a recorded gaze sequence, GRAZE synthesizes one grasp-and-lift motion offline. Our encoder GeoGaze maps
each gaze ray onto fixed Basis Point Set (BPS) points [ 35 ] , using ray closeness for local proximity
and displacement alignment for global direction. Cross-attention passes these cues to a diffusion Transformer. MANO fitting [ 37 ] and a contact refinement then turn the predicted hand vertices into grasps.

blocks.en: Our contributions are threefold. First, we formulate text-free, gaze-guided grasp-based HOI generation , in which recorded gaze replaces object and part names as the condition. On unseen objects, GRAZE grasps the target part more often than the strongest text baseline, especially on handles, which the text baselines rarely grasp even when the handle is named (Figs. c and 5 a). Gaze also conveys the approach side, which text leaves open: when the gaze is rotated around the object, the approach of GRAZE turns with it in 59.1% of the cases, against 20.5% for a text model retrained with clock words. With one distractor, a multi-object GRAZE picks the gazed object more often than a text baseline (47.4% vs. 15.3%, supplementary Tab. S4 ). Second, we propose Geometry-Aware Gaze Encoding (GeoGaze) , whose displacement-alignment term encodes the approach side. Third, we construct HOT3D-Grasp , a grasp-centered benchmark that extends HOT3D [ 2 ] with part annotations and object-disjoint three-fold splits for unseen objects.
blocks.zh: 我们的贡献有三个方面。 首先,我们制定无文本、有目光指引的、基于HOI的捕捉器,其中记录的目光取代物体和部分名称作为条件。 在隐形物体上,GRAZE比最强文本基线更经常地抓住目标部分,特别是在手柄上,即使手柄被命名,文本基线也很少抓住(图c和5a). Gaze还传达了接近的一面,文本留下了打开的一面:当视线围绕物体旋转时,GRAZE的接近在59.1%的情况下随它转动,而文本模型则有20.5%的时钟词重新训练. 使用一个分光器,一个多对象的GRAZE比文本基线更经常地选择被看到的对象(47.4%对15.3%,补充Tab. S4)。 第二,我们提出几何-Aware Gaze编码(GeoGaze),其迁移-对齐术语将接近方编码. 第三,我们构建HOT3D-Grasp,一个以抓取为中心的基准,将HOT3D[2]扩展,并配有部分说明和对象分离的三倍分割,用于未见物体.

blocks.en: 2 Related work
blocks.zh: 2 相关工作

blocks.en: Recent text-conditioned full-body human–object interaction methods jointly generate human and object motion, guided either by contact, as in HOI-Diff [ 33 ] , CG-HOI [ 12 ] , and CHOIS [ 23 ] , or by relational constraints, as in THOR [ 44 ] .
blocks.zh: 最近文字条件齐全的人体-物体相互作用方法共同产生人和物体的运动,或者以接触为导向,如HOI-Diff[33]、CG-HOI[12]和CHOIS[23],或者以关系限制为导向,如THOR[44]。

blocks.en: Hand–object methods emphasize articulated grasps and local contact [ 19 , 25 , 39 , 45 , 10 , 51 , 50 ] . Text2HOI predicts a text-conditioned surface contact map to guide diffusion and hand refinement [ 5 ] . DiffH2O [ 9 ] uses BPS object features [ 35 ] and separate diffusion models for grasping and manipulation. LatentHOI improves unseen-object generalization by generating global motion and grasp codes with diffusion. A GraspVAE decodes the grasp codes into articulated hands [ 24 ] . Text2Grasp studies object-part-conditioned static grasps [ 6 ] . LatentAct instead conditions on an explicit 3D contact point [ 34 ] . OpenHOI grounds open-vocabulary affordance regions with a 3D multimodal large language model (LLM) and conditions diffusion on these regions [ 53 ] .
blocks.zh: 手-目标方法强调清晰的把握和局部接触[19、25、39、45、10、51、50]。 Text2HOI预测一个文本条件的表面接触图,以指导扩散和手的精细化[5]. DiffH2O [9]使用BPS对象特征[35]和单独的传播模型来抓取和操纵. 后辈 HOI通过生成全球运动和以扩散方式抓住代码来改进隐形对象的泛化. GraspVAE将抓取代码解码成清晰的手 [24]. Text2Grasp 研究对象部分条件的静态抓取 [6]. 相反,Latent Act以一个明确的3D联络点为条件[34]. OpenHOI使用3D型多式联运大语言模型(LLM)并在这些地区传播条件[53].

blocks.en: Language provides semantic control but specifies the grasp region only indirectly, and even affordance grounding must infer the region from the wording. Moreover, neither language nor a contact point tells where the person is relative to the object, and this position decides from which side the hand reaches it. GRAZE instead grounds recorded gaze rays on object geometry. These rays start at the person’s eye and convey both the grasp region and the approach side.
blocks.zh: 语言提供了语义控制,但只是间接地规定了把握区域,甚至支付基础必须从措辞中推断出该区域。 此外,无论是语言还是联系点都无法说明人与物体的相对位置,这个位置决定手从哪一边到达它. GRAZE相反在物体几何学上记录了目光射线。 这些光线从人的眼睛开始,并传达到抓住区和接近方。

blocks.en: Most gaze-conditioned methods forecast future full-body motion from past motion and gaze. The MoGaze dataset shows that gaze helps predict pick-and-place intent [ 21 ] , and GazeMotion uses gaze to forecast body motion [ 17 ] . GIMO predicts future motion from past motion, 3D gaze, and the scene, exchanging information between gaze and motion branches [ 55 ] , and GazeMoDiff fuses gaze and observed motion with graph attention, then conditions diffusion through cross-attention [ 46 ] . These methods predict body motion and model neither hand articulation nor hand–object contact.
blocks.zh: 多数观察方法都预示着 未来的全身运动会从过去的运动和目光中产生 MoGaze数据集显示,凝视有助于预测采摘和放置意图[21],而GazeMotion使用凝视来预测身体运动[17]. GIMO从过去运动,3D凝视,以及场景中预测未来运动,在凝视和运动分支之间交换信息[55],GazeModiff导火线以图示注意的凝视和观察运动,然后通过交叉注意传播条件[46]. 这些方法预测身体运动和模型 既不是手发音,也不是手-物体接触。

blocks.en:
Closest to our setting, GHO-Diffusion synthesizes hand–object interaction from gaze: it represents each frame’s gaze by the inverse-distance-weighted feature of the nearest object point, aggregates these features with self-attention, and generates object motion and then hand motion [ 42 ] . GRAZE instead encodes gaze as ray closeness and displacement alignment over fixed BPS correspondences, and conditions the motion on these cues with cross-attention.
The concurrent Gaze2HOI [ 28 ] introduces the EgoAIM benchmark and forecasts the next second of egocentric interaction on HOT3D-Aria from observed video, gaze, and motion history. GRAZE instead synthesizes the full grasp-and-lift motion from 3D gaze rays over object geometry, without text or motion history.
blocks.zh:
最接近我们的设定, GHO- Diffusion 将手- 对象相互作用从视线中合成: 它通过最近物体点的反距离加权特征来代表每个帧的视线, 以自觉的方式把这些特性聚合起来, 并生成物体运动然后手动 [42] 。 GRAZE将视线编码为射线近距离和离散对准固定的BPS通信,并将这些提示上的动作设定为交叉注意。
Gaze2HOI [28] 介绍EgoAIM基准, GRAZE转而合成了3D视线对物体几何的完全把握和移动运动,没有文字或运动历史.

blocks.en: ObMan [ 15 ] , ContactPose [ 4 ] , and OakInk [ 47 ] provide static, contact-rich grasps, and HO-3D [ 14 ] , DexYCB [ 7 ] , GRAB [ 40 ] , H2O [ 22 ] , ARCTIC [ 13 ] , OakInk2 [ 48 ] , and TACO [ 26 ] provide dynamic 3D hand–object motion, but none of them records gaze.
blocks.zh: Obman [15], ContactPose [4],和OakInk [47] 提供静态的,富于接触的握手,HO-3D [14],DexYCB [7],GRAB [40],H2O [22],ARCTIC [13],OakInk2 [48],和TACO [26] 提供动态的3D手 - 物体运动,但都未记录有目视.

blocks.en: The GazeHOI dataset of GHO-Diffusion [ 42 ] records 3D gaze together with hand and object trajectories for task-level HOI synthesis. Its tasks emphasize target selection, rearrangement, and assembly rather than grasped parts, so the dataset is less suited to part-level grasp control. HOT3D [ 2 ] also pairs hand and object poses with eye gaze recorded by Aria glasses. From it we build HOT3D-Grasp, with grasp clips, part annotations, and object-disjoint splits for unseen objects.
blocks.zh: GHO-Diffusion[42]的GazeHOI数据集记录了3D凝视与手和物体轨迹,用于任务级HOI合成. 它的任务强调目标选择,重排,组装而不是抓取部分,因此数据集不太适合部分级抓取控制. HOT3D [2] 也用阿里亚眼镜录制的目光对手和物体的姿势. 我们从中构建HOT3D-Grasp,为看不见的物体配有抓取夹片,部分说明,以及对象分裂.

blocks.en: Gaze leads the hand: people fixate the object, often where they will grasp it, before the hand arrives [ 20 , 30 ] . The gaze that reveals the grasp intention therefore falls in the approach before contact. In HOT3D-Grasp, the hand first comes within 2 cm of the object at a median of 35% of the valid frames, and 88% of the first-30% gaze frames precede this point (supplementary Sec. S1.1 ). The remaining frames carry a zero gaze token, in training and at inference alike. For a model trained on all-frame gaze, giving only the first 30% at test time keeps grasp success and costs 2.1 part-accuracy points (supplementary Tab. S1 ).

blocks.en: MANO fitting converts the predicted vertices to MANO parameters. From the first predicted contact (hand within 2 cm of the object) onward, a contact refinement then adjusts the fitted hands for 300 steps with the penetration, displacement, and acceleration terms of BimArt [ 52 ] . blocks.en: We compare GRAZE with four text-conditioned HOI generation methods: Text2HOI [ 5 ] , DiffH2O [ 9 ] , LatentHOI [ 24 ] , and OpenHOI [ 53 ] . We train all baselines on each fold with their authors’ settings, including their refinement (Text2HOI and OpenHOI train a separate refiner). For OpenHOI, as in its authors’ recipe for a new dataset, we train the contact estimator and the generator and use the released affordance-tuned multimodal LLM. DiffH2O and LatentHOI do not take the clip length as a condition, so we set their output length to the clip length (supplementary Sec. S1.3 ). GHO-Diffusion [ 42 ] releases only a data toolkit, so we evaluate GHO-style gaze features on our backbone instead ( Sec. 4.4 , supplementary Tab. S9 ).

blocks.en: Grasp success: the Grasp Success Rate (GSR), our primary metric, counts a grasp as successful when the active hand touches the object (within 5 mm) in each of the final five valid frames and, at the final frame, penetrates it by at most 10 mm and has lifted it by at least 5 mm. Part grounding: Part Contact Precision (PCP), adapted from the contact precision of NL2Contact [ 54 ] , is the fraction of object points touched in the final frame that lie on the target part. Part Accuracy (Part Acc.), adapted from Text2Grasp [ 6 ] , is one when the target part holds the most touched points. Both are zero without contact. Physical plausibility: Interpenetration Depth (ID) measures how deep the hand enters the object [ 9 , 24 ] , averaged over the frames in which it penetrates. The final-contact rate (Contact) is the proportion of samples that meet the contact condition of GSR. For grasp stability, we fix the final hand and simulate the object under gravity [ 15 , 19 ] . Sim is the proportion of samples whose object moves less than 2 cm, and SimD is the mean object displacement (supplementary Sec. S4 ). Table 1 averages ten samples per test clip, and differences are tested with clip-level bootstrap 95% confidence intervals (CIs, n.s. if the interval includes zero).
blocks.zh: 格拉斯普成功:我们的主要衡量标准是格拉斯普成功率(GSR),当有效手触碰最后五个有效框架中每个框架的物体(在5毫米以内)时,将一个抓取算作成功,在最后框架时,最多穿透10毫米,并至少提升5毫米。 部分落地:部分接触精度(PCP),根据NL2Contact[54]的接触精度改编而成,是最终框架所触及的位于目标部分的对象点的一小部分. 部分准确性(Part Acc.),改编自Text2Grasp [6],是目标部分持有最触碰点时的一款. 两者均为零无接触. 物理可信度: 互通深度(ID)测量手进入物体的深度[9,24],平均在它穿透的帧上. 最后接触率(Contact)是符合GSR接触条件的样本比例. 为了把握稳定性,我们固定最后的手,在重力下模拟物体[15,19]. Sim是物体运动小于2厘米的样本比例,SimD是平均物体移位(subupmentary Sec. S4 .). 表1平均每个试验片段有10个样本,用剪切级的靴子夹95%的置信间隔(CIs,ns.如果间隔包括零)测试差异.

blocks.en: 4.4 What does gaze convey?
blocks.zh: 4.4 (中文(简体) ). 凝视传达什么?

blocks.en: We fix the backbone and the training recipe and vary only the condition: no condition, the target part label, the text prompt (CLIP-encoded [ 36 ] ), and other encodings of the same gaze (supplementary Tab. S9 ). Differences are significant unless marked n.s.
blocks.zh: 我们固定主干线和训练食谱,只改变条件:无条件,目标部分标签,文本提示(CLIP-encode [36]),以及同一目光的其他编码(补充Tab. S9 ). 除非标记不详,否则差异是显著的。

blocks.en: Gaze raises Part Acc. by 5.6 and PCP by 6.5 points over no condition and is not significantly different from the ground-truth part label. The gain is clearest on handles: a handle sticks out to one side, so a gaze toward that side indicates it (Part Acc. 26.1% vs. at most 18.0% without gaze, Fig. 5 a). Caps, rims, tops, and lids are harder: people also look at the top of an upright object in 84% of body grasps, so such gaze does not single out these parts. On these parts the text prompt is stronger (34.7% vs. 19.6%), and over all parts it is slightly ahead (52.2% vs. 49.3%, supplementary Sec. S5.2 ).
blocks.zh: 盖兹将Acc部分提升5.6分,五氯苯酚无条件提升6.5分,与地面真实部分标签没有显著区别。 在手柄上收益最为明显:把手柄伸到一边,因此对那一边的视线就表明了这一点(部分Acc.26.1%对最多18.0%的视线不放,图5a)。 盖子,轮圈,顶部和盖子都比较难:人们也会在84%的身体抓获量中看一个直立物体的顶部,所以这种视线不会单独列出这些部分. 在这些部分,文字提示更强烈(34.7%对19.6%),在所有部分中略为领先(52.2%对49.3%,补充S5.2%)。

blocks.en: Gaze also conveys the approach side, which the prompt and the part label omit. We rotate the recorded gaze around the object by 90 ∘ , 180 ∘ , and 270 ∘ , as if the person looked from another side. The final wrist of GRAZE turns with the rotation (within 45 ∘ ) for 59.1% of the rotated inputs, whereas LatentHOI retrained with clock words follows a changed word in only 20.5% (chance: 25%, Fig. 5 b, supplementary Sec. S5.2 and Fig. S5 ). The eye position alone carries much of the benefit: a model given only the eye-to-centroid ray (Head-only, supplementary Tab. S9 ) beats no condition (GSR + 4.1 +4.1 , Part Acc. + 4.3 +4.3 ). GRAZE leads it in GSR ( + 3.2 +3.2 ) but not in Part Acc. ( + 1.3 +1.3 , n.s.). The gaze direction matters on the 11% of clips whose gaze deviates from this ray by at least 10 ∘ : there, GRAZE exceeds Head-only by 19 GSR points. The raw ray and a GHO-style feature [ 42 ] follow the rotation less often than GRAZE (50.8% and 53.7% vs. 59.1%).

GRAZE在GSR(+3.2+3.2)中领先,但在Acc部分(+1.3+1.3,ns. 视线方向在视线偏离此射线的11%的片段上很重要。 仅以19GSR点数领先. 原射线和GHO型特征[42]遵循旋转频率低于GRAZE(50.8%和53.7%对59.1%)。

With one or two distractors, it contacts only the unseen target in 47.4% and 34.6% of the scenes, against 15.3% and 4.0% for Text2HOI extended to several objects and given the text prompt (supplementary Sec. S2.3 and Tab. S4 ).

(n.s.) and lets the approach follow a rotated gaze in 57.4% of the rotated inputs (gaze alone: 59.1%, n.s.), which a prompt alone cannot do. Adding the prompt to gaze raises PCP from 50.1% to 52.3%, the highest of all methods, and Part Acc. from 49.3% to 51.6% (n.s.).

blocks.en: 4.5 Robustness to gaze noise
blocks.zh: 4.5 凝视噪音的能力

blocks.en: Real eye tracking is imperfect, so we corrupt the recorded gaze at test time, without retraining. We either add random angular noise to every gaze direction (RMS error of 5 ∘ or 10 ∘ ), or drop each gaze frame with probability 0.2 or 0.5, which zeroes its gaze token. In every case, GSR and Part Acc. change by at most 1.1 points (n.s., supplementary Tab. S11 ).
blocks.zh: 真正的眼睛追踪是不完善的, 所以我们在测试时就破坏了记录的目光, 没有再培训。 我们要么在每个视线方向上添加随机角噪声(RMS错误为 5 QQ 或 10 QQ ),要么以概率 0.2 或 0.5 降下每个视线框,以零值表示其视线符号。 在每一种情况下,GSR和Part Acc的变动最多为1.1分(未另作补充的Tab.S11)。

blocks.en: 5 Conclusion
blocks.zh: 5 结论

blocks.en: We presented GRAZE, which generates grasp-and-lift motion from the first 30% of the recorded gaze instead of object and part names, together with HOT3D-Grasp, a benchmark with object-disjoint folds. On unseen objects, GRAZE grasped the target part more often than the strongest text baseline and achieved the highest grasp success. Without fine-tuning, it also achieved the highest grasp success on the GazeHOI dataset. Unlike the text models, it turned its approach with rotated gaze, and a multi-object variant selected the gazed object among distractors more often.
blocks.zh: 我们提出了GRAZE,它从录制的前30%的视线产生抓取和移动运动,而不是物体和部分名称,以及HOT3D-Grasp,一个带有物体离合折叠的基准. 在看不见的物体上,GRAZE比最强的文本基线更经常地抓住目标部分,并取得了最高的把握成功. 在没有微调的情况下,它还在GazeHOI数据集上取得了最高的把握成功. 与文本模型不同的是,它用旋转的目光扭转了它的方法,一个多对象的变体更经常地在分心器中选择了被目光的物体.

blocks.en: Gaze also has limits. People do not always look at the part they grasp, e.g . , at the top of an object grasped by its body. Adding a text prompt to gaze raised PCP, while gaze still set the approach side. Future work will fuse gaze and language more tightly when a prompt is available, generate motion online from a live eye tracker, and extend to gaze-driven pick-and-place in whole scenes.
blocks.zh: 盖兹亦有限. 人们并不总是看他们抓住的部分,例如,在被身体抓住的物体的顶部。 添加文字提示以凝视五氯苯酚升高,而凝视仍将接近点放在一边。 未来的工作将更紧密地将目光和语言融为一体,

blocks.en: S1.3 Cross-modal comparison and controls
blocks.zh: S1.3 跨模式比较和控制

blocks.en: The comparison between gaze and text is intentionally asymmetric in input modality but controlled in evaluation data ( Tab. S3 ). Text-conditioned methods receive object geometry and an explicit prompt containing the object and target part. The active hand (left, right, or both) is given to every method, as a per-hand flag for Text2HOI [ 5 ] , OpenHOI [ 53 ] , and GRAZE, and through the prompt for DiffH2O [ 9 ] and LatentHOI [ 24 ] . GRAZE receives the same object geometry and the recorded gaze of the first 30% of the frames, without object- or target-part text. Only GRAZE and its same-backbone controls ( Tabs. S9 and S10 ) also receive the first-frame object pose, which serves only to express the gaze in the object frame and to place the generated motion in the scene. All methods are evaluated on the same clips and object geometries. The experiment tests whether gaze, without object or part text, conveys the part that a prompt names and the approach side that it leaves open.

blocks.en:
DiffH2O and LatentHOI are originally formulated with separate grasping and
manipulation stages. For DiffH2O, we train the authors’ full model in its one-stage configuration with short text prompts (its “simple annotations”) on each fold and refer to this model as DiffH2O throughout. For LatentHOI, we train its complete model with the released code on each fold. Neither method takes the clip length as an explicit condition: DiffH2O generates a clip-length motion with its official zero mask, and the fixed 96-frame output of LatentHOI is resampled in time to the clip length, so that each is judged on the end state of its own motion. We introduce no further adaptation of either two-stage method. In contrast, Text2HOI has no explicit grasp–manipulation stage
separation, so we train its full model directly on our benchmark. We convert
the final motions from all methods to a common hand–object representation and
compute all reported comparison metrics with the same evaluator, thresholds,
frame masks, and object meshes.
OpenHOI [ 53 ] adds an object affordance map, predicted by a multimodal large language model (LLM) from the prompt, to the Text2HOI contact estimator and generator. We compute the affordance maps with the released affordance-tuned multimodal LLM and, following the authors’ recipe for a new HOI dataset, train the contact estimator and the generator on each fold. The maps separate parts on only 4 of the 21 objects whose clips grasp two or more different parts. On the other 17 objects they barely depend on the part name (median correlation 0.99 between maps for different part names). On most objects, OpenHOI thus behaves like Text2HOI with a weak part cue, consistent with its lower scores in Tab. 1 of the main paper. To rule out a reproduction error, we follow the released configuration and train the generator for as many epochs as the Text2HOI generator on which it is built. On every fold it reaches a training loss similar to that of Text2HOI, so its lower scores do not come from failed training.
blocks.zh:
diffH2O 和 Lateent 数据 HOI最初是用单独的抓取和
操作阶段。 对于DiffH2O,我们用短文本提示(它的“简单说明”)来训练作者的完整模式的单阶段配置,并将这个模式称为DiffH2O。 给列梯 HOI,我们训练它的完整的模型,每个折叠上都有释放的代码. 两种方法都不以剪辑长度为明确条件: DiffH2O 以其正式的零掩码生成一个剪长运动,以及Latet的固定96帧输出 HOI被及时重印到剪辑长度,这样每个都根据自己运动的结束状态来判断. 我们不再采用两个阶段的方法。 反之,Text2HOI没有明确的把握-操纵阶段
分离,所以我们直接用基准来训练它的全部模型。 我们皈依
最后动议,从所有方法到共同的手 - 对象陈述和
计算所有报告的与同一评价员的比较指标、阈值、
套装面具, 和物体 meshes。
OpenHOI [53] 在Text2HOI的接触估计器和生成器中增加了一个对象承受力图,该图是由一个多模式大语言模型(LLM)从提示器预言的. 我们用发行的付费调制多式LLM来计算支付率地图,并按照作者对新的HOI数据集的配方,在每个折叠上训练联系估计器和生成器。 在21个物体中,只有4个物体的剪辑抓住了两个或两个以上不同的部分,这些地图将其中的部分分开。 在另外17个物体上,它们几乎不依赖于部分名称(不同部分名称的地图之间的中间相关性0.99). 在大多数对象上,OpenHOI因此表现得像Text2HOI带有弱的部分提示,与它在Tab中的较低分数一致. 主报一. 为了排除复制错误,我们遵循释放的配置,并训练生成器的时代与它所建的Text2HOI生成器一样多. 在每个折叠上,它都达到了类似于Text2HOI的训练损失,因此其较低的分数并不来自于训练失败.

blocks.en: Two measurements show where the baselines fall short in Tab. 1 of the main paper. First, the baselines mostly fail before the grasp is complete. The active hand is not in contact through the final five frames in 30.3% of the samples of Text2HOI, 55.3% of DiffH2O, 31.5% of LatentHOI, and 45.8% of OpenHOI, against 1.9% for GRAZE, whose GSR failures are mostly final-frame penetration above 10 mm (26.7% of the samples, while Fig. S6 shows a smaller penetration share because its taxonomy assigns wrong-part grasps before penetration). Second, the text-conditioned baselines ground the named part far better on objects seen in training. From the subject-disjoint folds ( Tab. S13 ), where every test object is seen, to the object folds, Part Acc. falls from 71.7% to 36.8% for Text2HOI, from 60.9% to 31.7% for DiffH2O, and from 69.7% to 43.6% for LatentHOI, against 59.2% to 49.3% for GRAZE. This is consistent with a part name being learned together with the shapes of the training objects, whereas gaze marks the location on the new object itself.

blocks.en: S1.4 Zero-shot GazeHOI protocol
blocks.zh: S1.4 零射门 GazeHOI 协议

blocks.en: We convert GazeHOI [ 42 ] to the format of HOT3D-Grasp and give the same converted data to every method. Each clip runs from 12 frames before the first hand–object contact to 11 frames after the lift onset (at most 99 frames, median 45). The hand parameters are converted to our MANO layer, and the scene and the object meshes are rotated so that their world-up direction matches that of HOT3D. The evaluation set contains 939 clips of 36 objects from 194 recordings: every clip of both GazeHOI splits in which the recorded gaze ray comes within 1 cm of the object, i.e . , the 94 clips of 28 objects of the test split and 845 clips of the training split. No evaluated model is trained on GazeHOI, so both splits are unseen by every method. Each method generates one sample per clip. GazeHOI has no part annotation, and its prompts name the hand but neither the object nor a part ( e.g . , “Grab this with right hand.”), so every text baseline receives this prompt (GRAZE receives only the gaze and the same hand flag) and Part Acc. and PCP are not reported. The three object-fold models of Tab. 1 are applied without fine-tuning, and we report the mean over the three models. GRAZE uses the gaze of the first 30% of the frames, as on HOT3D. Adding a part word to this prompt does not help the strongest baseline: on the 94 test-split clips, with four samples per clip, LatentHOI reaches a GSR of 30.5% with the original prompt, 29.9% with “Grab body of this with …” (n.s.), and 23.0% with “Grab handle of this with …” (significantly lower).
blocks.zh: 我们把 GazeHOI [42] 转换为 HOT3D-Grasp 格式,并将相同的转换数据给每个方法. 每段剪辑从第一手-物体接触前的12帧到升起后11帧(最多99帧,中位数45). 手的参数被转换到我们的MANO层,场景和物体的中间体被旋转,使其世界上升方向与HOT3D的一致. 评估套装有194个录音中的36个物体的939个片段:每段记录的凝视射线在物体1厘米以内分解的GazeHOI两个片段,即试验分解的28个物体的94个片段和训练分解的845个片段. 没有经过评价的模型在GazeHOI上受过训练,所以这两种分裂都用每一种方法都看不见. 每种方法每个片段产生一个样本. GazeHOI没有部分注释,其提示点名指向手,但指向物体或部分(例如“用右手标注”),因此每个文本基线都收到这个提示点(GRAZE只收到眼睛和同一手旗),部分Acc.和五氯苯酚没有报告。 Tab的三个对象倍模型. 1的应用没有微调,我们报告三个模型的平均值。 GRAZE在HOT3D上使用前30%帧的视线. 在此提示中添加一个部分字无助于最强的基准:在94个试验片段上,每个片段有4个样本,LatentHOI在原始提示中达到30.5%的GSR,在29.9%的GSR中,“这个带的物体......”(不详),在23.0%的Grab处理器中,......(大大降低)。

blocks.en: S2.2 Geometry-aware gaze features
blocks.zh: S2.2 几何感知视力特征

blocks.en: For every valid frame and BPS index, GeoGaze retains two separate values: ray closeness (a Gaussian of the distance from the nearest object point 𝐪 k \mathbf{q}_{k} of the basis point to the forward gaze ray) and displacement alignment (the cosine between the gaze direction and the BPS displacement ϕ k \boldsymbol{\phi}_{k} , rescaled to [ 0 , 1 ] [0,1] ). Closeness uses the gaze origin and direction and remains nonzero when a noisy ray passes near, rather than through, a small object. Alignment uses the direction only and remains defined without an intersection. It encodes the viewing direction in the object frame, not where the ray lands. The two K K -dimensional fields of a frame are concatenated before the gaze projection, so each frame contributes one gaze token in which the closeness and alignment entries keep separate projection weights.
blocks.zh: 对于每一个有效的帧和BPS指数,GeoGaze保留了两个独立的值:射线近距离(距离最近的对象点q k\mathbf{q}_{k}距离前视线的基点q k\mathb{q}_{k})和离位对齐(视线方向与BPS离位的余弦X k\boldsymbol\phi}_{k},调整为[0,1] [0,1]). 近距离利用凝视的源头和方向,当一个吵吵的射线经过一个小物体而不是穿过这个物体时,则保持非零. 对齐只使用方向,并且保持不变,没有交叉点。 它将视线方向编码在物体框中,而不是射线降落的地方. 一个帧的两个K-维域在凝视投影之前被调和,因此每个帧都贡献了一个凝视符,其中近和对齐的条目保持单独的投影权重.

A field whose maximum falls below 0.1 carries almost no signal. This happens for 23% of clips at σ = 0.05 \sigma=0.05 but only 8% at σ = 0.15 \sigma=0.15 . blocks.en: S2.3 Multi-object slots
blocks.zh: S2.3 多对象槽

blocks.en: Each test scene of the three object folds places the recorded target, an object unseen in training, together with one distractor (two-object setting) or two distractors (three-object setting), drawn from seen and unseen objects. Each setting has one scene per clip (912 scenes). Target Selection Accuracy (TSA) is the proportion of scenes in which the hand contacts the target and no distractor. Distractor Contact Rate (DCR) is the proportion in which it contacts any distractor, so TSA + + DCR ≤ \leq 100 (contact as defined for multi-object evaluation in Sec. S4 : at least two active-hand keypoints within 2 cm). Held is the proportion of scenes whose hand still holds the target in the final five frames.
blocks.zh: 三个物体折叠的每个试验场景都将记录的目标,一个在训练中看不见的物体,连同一个分心器(双物体设置)或两个分心器(三物体设置),从所看到和看不见的物体中抽取. 每个设定每个片段有一个场景(912场). 目标选择精确度(TSA)是手接触目标且没有分散注意力的场景比例. 干扰器接触率(DCR)是它接触任何转移器的比例,所以TSA + + DCR →\leq 100(Sec. S4中多对象评价的接触定义:在2厘米内至少有两个活动手键点). 持有的是手在最后五帧中仍然持有目标的场景比例.

blocks.en: For Q Q candidates, the object encoder and GeoGaze share weights across candidates. Candidate-specific gaze and object features remain in their own slots, while the global object condition is obtained by mean pooling. Two-object training pairs the target with a context object present in the same HOT3D recording and randomly permutes their slot order. The context slot retains its recorded trajectory, and reconstruction losses supervise every object slot. There is no explicit collision loss or target-index embedding. The hand streams attend to all candidate gaze features, so the model must infer which candidate is the target from where the gaze falls relative to each candidate’s geometry. The same parameters are used for every slot, allowing zero-shot three-candidate evaluation without new learned parameters.
blocks.zh: 对于Q候选人,对象编码器和GeoGaze在候选人之间共享权重. 候选人特定视线和对象特征仍然留在自己的槽中,而全局对象条件则通过平均集合获得. 双对象训练将目标与同一HOT3D录制中存在的上下文对象对齐,并随机地固定他们的槽顺序. 上下文槽保留其记录的轨迹,重建损失监督每个对象槽. 没有明显的碰撞损失或目标索引嵌入。 手流关注所有候选人的目光特征,因此模型必须推断哪个候选人是相对于每个候选人几何特征的目光下降的目标。 每个插槽都使用相同的参数,允许零镜头的3个扫描评价,没有新的学习参数.

The original object input becomes slot 1,
and an identically encoded candidate is concatenated as slot 2. Each slot
receives its own PointNet geometry, scale, centroid, trajectory token, and
slot-aligned contact-map embedding. The target slot receives the prompt-derived
contact map and the context slot a zero map. As with GRAZE, the two-slot model is evaluated with a
third slot that reuses the slot weights, without fine-tuning.
On the three object folds, Text2HOI ∗ is trained for about 9,000 epochs and the GRAZE multi-object model for 4,000 epochs, so the gaze model receives fewer updates.

blocks.en: We compare with Text2HOI only: its point-cloud object encoder and contact estimator take each additional candidate as one more object slot with minimal changes to the architecture (denoted Text2HOI ∗ ), whereas DiffH2O and LatentHOI condition on a single object and would need a structural redesign. Table S4 reports one trained model per method and fold, averaged over the three folds. GRAZE receives the first 30% of the gaze frames. GRAZE uses its contact refinement, applied to the union of the candidate surfaces. For a fair comparison we also apply the nearest-point refinement of Tab. S6 , likewise on the union of the candidate surfaces, to Text2HOI ∗ . The refinement leaves the scores of Text2HOI ∗ almost unchanged (within 0.7 points), because it moves only the hands and Text2HOI ∗ already contacts a distractor in most scenes. GRAZE more often contacts the target alone than Text2HOI ∗ does, touches a distractor less often, and holds the target at the end about twice (two objects) and four times (three objects) as often, but it stays far below the recorded motion. Text2HOI ∗ moves its distractors by more than 1 cm in 98–99% of the two-object scenes across the three folds (GRAZE: 26–29%), so its DCR partly reflects the distractor motion it generates.
blocks.zh: 我们只与Text2HOI比较:它的点-云对象编码器和联系人估计器将每个额外的候选对象作为另一个对象槽,对架构的修改最小(注意Text2HOI *),而DiffH2O和LatentHOI条件在一个单一对象上,需要结构重新设计. 表S4报告每个方法和折叠一个训练有素的模型,平均在三个折叠上。 GRAZE获得前30%的视框. GRAZE比Text2HOI ∗ 更经常地单独接触目标,接触分散器的次数较少,并在结尾时将目标保持了大约两次(两个物体)和四次(三个物体)的频率,但远远低于记录的运动. Text2HOI ∗ 在98–99 %的双对象场景中将它的分光器移动超过1cm,跨越三个折叠(GRAZE:26–29 %),所以它的DCR部分反映了它产生的分光器运动.

blocks.en: S3 Implementation and reproducibility
blocks.zh: S3 实施和可复制

blocks.en: Because the network predicts vertices rather than MANO parameters, we fit MANO pose, translation, and shape to the M = 100 M=100 predicted vertices of each hand using vertex matching with weak pose, shape, and temporal regularization. We then apply a deterministic contact refinement. Neither stage is learned, and neither uses ground-truth hand pose or ground-truth contact.
blocks.zh: 因为网络预测的是顶点而不是MANO参数,所以我们把MANO的姿势,翻译,和形状配合到M=100M=100的每只手的预测顶点,使用顶点与弱的姿势,形状,以及时间的调节相匹配. 然后我们采用确定性的联系方法。 两个阶段都没有经验,也没有使用地面真实的手姿或地面真实的接触。

blocks.en:
MANO fitting uses 80 Adam iterations with learning rate 0.05, pose
and shape regularization 10 − 4 10^{-4} , and pose- and translation-temporal
regularization 10 − 3 10^{-3} .
The contact refinement then optimizes the fitted mesh for 300 AdamW steps at learning rate 5 × 10 − 4 5\times 10^{-4} with the BimArt [ 52 ] penetration, displacement, and acceleration terms weighted 10, 100, and 1,000. A frame counts as in contact when the predicted hand comes within 2 cm of the object. The refinement runs from the first predicted contact to the end of the valid sequence with a five-frame transition and uses the last ten valid frames when no contact is predicted.
All GRAZE variants use these fixed values.
blocks.zh:
MANO装配使用80个亚当迭代,学习率0.05,姿势
正规化 10 - 4 10 - 4 - 4 10 - 4] , 以及假名和翻译时态
正规化 10 - 3 10 - 3] .
接触精细化后,以5×10−4 5\times 10×4}的学习速率,优化了300 AdamW步的装网,采用BimArt[52]的渗透、移动和加速度值加权10、100和1000。 当预测的手在物体2厘米以内时,一个帧算作接触中. 完善从第一个预测的接触到有五帧过渡的有效序列的结束,在没有预测接触时使用最后十个有效帧.
所有GRAZE变体都使用这些固定值.

blocks.en:
All baselines are trained from scratch on the corresponding HOT3D-Grasp split (OpenHOI keeps its released affordance-tuned multimodal LLM),
using the optimization budgets of their original configurations where released.
Text2HOI uses 30,000 generator, 10,000 contact-estimator, and 3,000 refiner iterations at batch size 64. DiffH2O uses 400,000 iterations, and
LatentHOI uses
15 epochs for its grasp VAE followed by 1,250 epochs for latent diffusion. The OpenHOI generator is trained for as many epochs as that of Text2HOI. We change the
data interface and use the one-stage configuration of DiffH2O ( Sec. S1.3 ), but do not shorten a
baseline merely to match our training time.

所有基线都从零开始在相应的HOT3D-Grasp拆分(OpenHOI保持其释放的支付率调制多式联运LLM)上训练,
使用发布时其原始配置的优化预算。

使用 LatenTHOI 软件
15个抓住VAE的时代,然后是1 250个潜在扩散的时代。 OpenHOI生成器的训练对象与Text2HOI一样多. 我们改变
数据接口和使用DiffH2O(Sec.S1.3)的单阶段配置,但不缩短
基线只是为了适应我们的训练时间。

blocks.en: The diffusion Transformer has 8 layers with latent dimension D = 512 D=512 , feed-forward dimension 1,024, 4 attention heads, and dropout 0.1. For training stability, we apply a 10% gaze-condition dropout, which replaces the whole gaze condition of a sample with the zero gaze token. The model is trained with AdamW [ 27 ] (learning rate 10 − 4 10^{-4} , weight decay 10 − 2 10^{-2} , batch size 64) under a 1,000-step cosine diffusion schedule [ 31 ] , and sampling uses all 1,000 steps. blocks.en: We follow the simulation-displacement protocol of ObMan [ 15 ] , reused by GraspTTA [ 19 ] , and port its reference PyBullet [ 11 ] settings unchanged. Each sample is simulated once at its final valid frame, the frame at which GSR is evaluated, with the hand and object in the evaluator’s world frame. The final MANO hand mesh is a static, massless concave triangle mesh. The object is a dynamic body built from a V-HACD [ 29 ] convex decomposition of its mesh, with a mass of 1 kg and its center of mass at the mean of the mesh vertices. Gravity of 9.8 m/s 2 acts against the HOT3D world-up direction. The simulation runs for 35 steps of 1/240 s (0.146 s), and no table or other support is present. SimD is the distance between the initial and final object center of mass, averaged over all samples. Sim is the proportion of samples displaced by less than 2 cm. An object that touches no hand falls freely, about 10.7 cm in this duration, and is kept in both averages. ObMan notes that balanced penetration forces can also hold an object, so Sim and SimD are read together with ID. Among the samples in contact whose final-frame penetration depth is at most 10 mm, GRAZE holds the object in 80.8% of the cases, against at most 70.4% for the baselines, whereas above 10 mm LatentHOI is slightly more stable (67.8% vs. 63.1%). Run on the recorded motions, the same protocol gives Sim 73.9% and SimD 2.04 cm over the three object folds, which serves as a reference for the generated grasps.

SimD是质量的初始物体中心与最终物体中心之间的距离,在所有样本上均值. Sim是流离2厘米以下的样本比例. 不接触手的物体在这个期间会自由落下,约10.7厘米,并保存在两个平均值中. blocks.en: Table 1 of the main paper evaluates each baseline with its released pipeline, and Tab. S6 adds the nearest-point refinement to every baseline and separates its effect. With nearest-point displacements, this refinement raises GSR by 2.5 to 9.0 points for every baseline and by 6.7 points for the MANO fit of GRAZE. It raises Part Acc. by 1.0 to 2.5 points for all five. GRAZE’s own refinement adds 25.7 GSR and 11.7 Part Acc. points to the same MANO fit. The difference comes from what the network predicts: GRAZE outputs sampled hand vertices with their displacement vectors to the object instead of MANO parameters, and its refinement uses these predicted displacements as contact targets, whereas the nearest-point version sees only the fitted mesh. With nearest-point displacements on both, LatentHOI exceeds GRAZE by 8.3 GSR and 4.7 Part Acc. points (95% CIs [ 5.0 , 11.5 ] [5.0,11.5] and [ 1.6 , 7.9 ] [1.6,7.9] ), so the results of GRAZE rely on its predicted displacements. The refinement also lowers ID in every row. Table S7 lists the per-fold values behind Tab. 1 of the main paper and Tabs. S6 , S9 , and S10 .

blocks.en: The rows of Tab. S9 differ only in the condition. Text prompt is the sentence the text baselines receive ( e.g . , “Grab cap of bottle_bbq with right hand.”), encoded by the frozen CLIP [ 36 ] text encoder, and Part label gives the ground-truth part as input. Raw ray gives the gaze origin and direction unchanged. Gaze point keeps, per frame, only the object point nearest the gaze ray, without eye position or direction. Head-only is trained and tested with only the ray from the eye to the object centroid, without the gaze direction. GHO-style, a simplified input after GHO-Diffusion [ 42 ] , gives the eye ray with the object point nearest to it and their distance, without the inverse-distance weighting and self-attention aggregation of GHO-Diffusion. With the rotated gaze of Sec. 4.4 of the main paper, Head-only, the raw ray, and the GHO-style feature all follow the rotation less often than GeoGaze (54.6%, 50.8%, and 53.7% vs. 59.1%, all significant). Head-only already improves over no condition (GSR + 4.1 +4.1 [ 1.3 , 6.8 ] [1.3,6.8] , Part Acc. + 4.3 +4.3 [ 2.1 , 6.5 ] [2.1,6.5] , PCP + 5.1 +5.1 [ 3.3 , 6.9 ] [3.3,6.9] , all significant). GeoGaze leads Head-only in GSR ( + 3.2 +3.2 , [ 0.2 , 6.3 ] [0.2,6.3] , significant) but not in Part Acc. ( + 1.3 +1.3 , [ − 1.3 , 4.0 ] [-1.3,4.0] ) or PCP ( + 1.3 +1.3 , [ − 0.8 , 3.4 ] [-0.8,3.4] ), both not significant. The gaze direction matters when the gaze leaves the object center: on the 11% of clips (99) whose gaze deviates from the eye-to-centroid ray by at least 10 ∘ , GeoGaze reaches a 19-point higher GSR than Head-only (95% CI [ 8.2 , 29.3 ] [8.2,29.3] , 2,000 bootstrap resamples), with no significant change in Part Acc.

blocks.en: Clock words are defined in the frame of each object, so that they need no world pose. The up axis is the signed mesh axis ( ± x \pm x , ± y \pm y , or ± z \pm z ) that points closest to the world-up direction in most clips of the object. Twelve o’clock is the positive direction of the next mesh axis in the cyclic order x → y → z → x x\to y\to z\to x , and 3 o’clock lies 90 ∘ clockwise from it when seen from above. The recorded direction of a clip is the azimuth of the active-hand center at the first contact frame around this up axis, assigned to the nearest of the four clock positions. LatentHOI and our backbone with the text prompt are retrained on every object fold with “, approaching from N o’clock” appended to each training prompt, where N is the recorded direction. Clips in which both hands act are excluded. Follow is computed on the remaining 848 single-hand clips of the three object folds for every method, with four samples per clip. At test time, every clip receives the recorded word and the three words rotated by 90 ∘ , 180 ∘ , and 270 ∘ . For GRAZE, the recorded gaze rays are instead rotated by the same angles about the up axis of the object through its first-frame centroid. An output follows the rotation when its final-wrist azimuth, relative to the output for the unrotated input with the same sampling noise, has turned by the rotation angle to within ± \pm 45 ∘ . Fig. 5 b of the main paper further splits the remaining outputs: one that stayed within 45 ∘ of the output for the unrotated input did not turn, and every other one turned elsewhere. Classifier-free guidance at inference (scale 2.5, as in LatentHOI) does not make our backbone follow the clock word: it follows the rotation in 2.2% of the rotated inputs with and without guidance, although guidance changes the outputs (median final-wrist change 14–19 ∘ across the three folds).

blocks.en: The prompts of the text baselines are short, which could put them at a disadvantage against a per-frame gaze input. DiffH2O [ 9 ] shows that more detailed text descriptions give finer control over the generated interaction. Its descriptions detail the sequence of actions. Our task, however, is a single grasp, so we instead detail how the hand grips the object. We retrain LatentHOI with such a prompt: each prompt gets an added sentence that names the fingers holding the object, derived from the recorded contact of the same clip ( e.g . , “The thumb and index finger pinch it.”). The added detail does not help: on the three object folds (own pipeline, as in Tab. 1 of the main paper), GSR is unchanged (46.6% vs. 46.6%, 95% CI of the difference [ − 2.1 , 2.1 ] [-2.1,2.1] ), and Part Acc. and PCP fall (41.6% vs. 43.6% and 40.1% vs. 42.5%).

blocks.en: Five of the 31 objects have a single annotated part. On their 103 clips, Part Acc. and PCP are one whenever the final grasp touches the object, so these clips measure contact and not the choice of part. Table S12 therefore recomputes both metrics for the rows of Tab. 1 of the main paper without these objects (809 clips, 26 objects, and 54 object–part pairs over the three folds) in three ways: averaged over clips (Micro), over objects (Obj.), and over object–part pairs (Pair). Removing the one-part objects lowers the clip average of every method by 2.0 to 6.1 points, and GRAZE keeps the highest value in every column. Under an object-level bootstrap, GRAZE significantly exceeds Text2HOI with the nearest-point refinement in five of the six Micro, Obj., and Pair columns, whereas its margin over LatentHOI with the nearest-point refinement (1.4 to 5.6 points) is not significant.

blocks.en:
Figure S6 assigns every generated sample of the three object folds
to exactly one outcome, checked in this order: no contact (the hand never touches the object),
contact lost (the hand touches the object but not in all of the final five frames), final contact on a non-target part,
final-frame penetration deeper than 10 mm, and target-part success (contact with the target
part throughout the final five frames and final-frame penetration depth ≤ \leq 10 mm). GRAZE reaches the object far more reliably than
the text-conditioned baselines, but, once the target part is required, its dominant failure is a grasp on the wrong
part. On the dumbbell, the flask, the patterned mug, and the vase almost every failure is such a grasp, and penetration concentrates on the birdhouse toy and the dino toy. In 68% of the wrong-part grasps of GRAZE, the recorded gaze before first contact falls mostly on a part other than the target, against 32% for its target-part successes.

blocks.en: GRAZE is trained on single-object grasp-and-lift clips from nine HOT3D subjects (912 clips, 31 objects) and is tested outside HOT3D only zero-shot on GazeHOI. Motions beyond grasping are not covered. Wrong-part grasps remain the main failure mode ( Fig. S6 ), and the generator, trained from motion data without a physics simulator, can still form contact through penetration, which ID and Sim measure. Clip boundaries and part labels are manual annotations, and the study is offline, without a user evaluation.
blocks.zh: GRAZE从9个HOT3D主题(912个短片,31个对象)中接受单对象抓取和升起夹片的训练,并在HOT3D外仅对GazeHOI进行零射试. 无法掌握的动议没有被涵盖。 错段抓取仍然是主要故障模式(图S6),从运动数据中训练而无物理模拟器的生成器仍然可以通过穿透而形成接触,这种接触是ID和Sim测量的. 剪贴边框和部分标签是手动说明,研究是离线的,没有用户评价.

blocks.en:
The evaluation uses recorded gaze from HOT3D and GazeHOI and does not cover gaze-tracking
latency or a user in a closed loop with the generator.
Gaze should also be treated as an optional interface rather than a universal
replacement for language or other accessibility-oriented controls.
